#### §3: Memory allocation

| ID | Spec | Ann. | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-3.1 | §3.1 | — | **Two allocation domains.** Library-internal memory uses the internal heap directly. Memory handed to C callers (`strdup`, `getline`, `open_memstream`, `asprintf`, `scandir`, ...) comes from the *exported, interposable* `malloc` through the PLT, so that a user-interposed `free` can release it (spec §3.3; F23). |
| D-3.2 | §3.1 | ARB, HIST | `malloc(0)` returns a unique freeable pointer. `realloc(p, 0)` frees and returns NULL. Both are the contract's glibc choices, kept for compatibility. |
| D-3.3 | §3.1 | HIST | Internal deallocation passes size and alignment (`free_sized`-style), so there is no per-block header for internal allocations. C `free(p)` recovers the size from the size-class map. |
| D-3.4 | §3.2 | HIST, COMPAT | Introspection is implementation-neutral. `mallinfo2` reports in-use, held and releasable bytes in the fields whose meaning is neutral, and zero elsewhere (observable). A block freed by another thread counts as free once its `free` has returned, collected by its owner or not (D-3.11), in every report (`mallinfo2`, `mallinfo`, `malloc_stats`, `malloc_info`): the reader subtracts pending remote frees, so the result does not depend on when collection runs. `mallinfo` saturates at `INT_MAX` instead of wrapping (observable, stricter). `mallopt` returns 1 for every parameter, known or not, as glibc (owner ruling 2026-10-22, #412), and 0 only for `M_MXFAST` outside 0 to 160; only `M_PERTURB` takes effect, the others are ignored. `malloc_info` emits the same XML element structure with neutral content. |
| D-3.5 | §3.3 | HIST | The hook variables are inert compat data (as in 2.34+). `mcheck`/`mtrace` semantics come with the debug library (phase 13). `malloc_get_state`/`malloc_set_state` fail. **Phase 13 (owner ruling 2026-10-04: kept; phase 14 ships an empty `libc_malloc_debug.so.0`, and preloading it gives no hooks):** Liella's libc provides the `libc_malloc_debug` semantics itself (`mcheck`, `mcheck_pedantic`, `mprobe`, `mcheck_check_all`, `mtrace` with `MALLOC_TRACE` read through `secure_getenv` and never written in a secure process, `M_PERTURB`): checked blocks carry 16 guard bytes before and 8 after, tracked in a library-owned table; `mcheck` succeeds only before the first block the C family hands out; a freed block reports `MCHECK_FREE`; the mtrace log follows the reference's format. Off, the cost is one relaxed load of one atomic word per call (`Heap::alloc`/`free` are `#[inline(always)]` so the check does not stop the fast path being inlined: 13.7 ns per 64-byte pair). The hook variables stay inert. `malloc_info` options other than 0 give -1 `EINVAL` (malloc_info(3), §3.2 since 2026-10-04; glibc returns 22); `malloc_trim` returns 1 only when pages were released; `mallopt` returns 0 for parameters it does not honour (D-3.4). |
| D-3.6 | §3.5 | HIST | **Internal:** `Arena` (obstack semantics) returns `Result`. **Boundary:** `obstack_alloc_failed_handler` (default: exit) is called by the legacy adapter, per the contract. |
| D-3.7 | §3.7 | HIST | The allocator never uses `brk`: pages come from `mmap` only. So `brk`/`sbrk` (thin wrappers) cannot corrupt the heap (observable: no interaction with `malloc`). |
| D-3.8 | §3.4 | HIST | `alloca` is a compiler builtin. Nothing to implement. |
| D-3.9 | §3.1 | — | **S8 is enforced by lint.** `clippy.toml` lists the infallible `alloc` methods (`Vec::push`, `with_capacity`, `reserve`, `extend_from_slice`, `insert`, `resize`, `append`, `vec![x; n]`, `Box::new`, `String::push_str`, `to_vec`, `to_owned`, `Extend::extend`, ...). Every library crate root denies `clippy::disallowed_methods` outside tests. Host tools (`xtask`, build scripts) and tests are exempt. **Accepted by the owner (2026-10-01).** **Manual review obligations**, since no lint can catch them: (1) `Iterator::collect` into a `Vec`, `String` or other collection; (2) `format!` and `alloc::fmt::format`; (3) `Clone` of a collection (`Vec`, `String`, `Box`). In library code each of these is either replaced by a fallible equivalent (`TryVec::from_slice`, `try_clone`, a fallible collect helper) or carries a comment explaining why it cannot fail. Every review of a library crate checks for all three. |
| D-3.17 | §3.1 | — | **`realloc` resizes with one lookup** (REALLOC-ONE-LOOKUP, TIMING-COV-REALLOC-GROW-NONAVX2, ruling #3389). `Heap::fit(pages, addr, size)` finds the block once, through the slab hint, and returns `Same(usable)` (the block already serves the request), `Held(Held{class, index})` (it must move; the block is already located) or `Other` (not a small block). It replaces `fits_in_place` and covers `0 < size <= MAX_SMALL` (was `<= 1 KiB`). `Heap::resize_held` moves a `Held` block without a second lookup: it takes a block from the target class with `alloc_hint`, copies, clears the old bit and calls `freed_into`; any miss falls back to `resize_slow`. `Heap::resize` is `fit`, then `resize_held` or `resize_slow`. The target size comes from `move_target`, the general path's forecast rule, which `resize_slow` now uses too, so a move copies once. Size 0 inside `resize` (reachable only through `malloc_debug`) takes `resize_slow`; the result is unchanged (class 0 stays in place, any other class gets a class 0 block). Exports: `realloc` and `__libc_realloc` return `p` with no stack frame on `Same`; `Held` goes to `realloc_held` (`#[inline(never)]`); `Other` goes to `realloc_general`. **Rules kept unchanged:** up to 1 KiB the stay-in-place rule is `HALF_BELOW` (PERF-REALLOC-USABLE-3); above 1 KiB `keeps_in_place` applies, the general path's own rule, so requests above `FORECAST_CAP` no longer take the locate, general alloc, general free route. Observable results (returned pointer, contents, `errno`) are unchanged. Was: the entry's in-place test found the block and failed, then `realloc_general` found it again in `Heap::resize` (32 B grow: 201 instructions, 59 + 130 + 12 copy; 2048 B: 467, of which 265 in `resize_slow`). Measured (`wl_percall` `realloc_grow_x2`, Broadwell-EP host, instructions per call): AVX2 dispatch glibc 199.5, before 252.9, after 209.8 (1.05 of glibc); non-AVX2 (`hwcaps=-AVX2`) before 288.8, after 245.7 (1.23); the gap left is the non-AVX2 copy of 1 to 2 KiB blocks, not changed here. Gate on 96b75b97: 8810 passed, 0 failed, conformance 11/11; four plants caught (copy one short, grow past usable, keep-big always true, alloc into the old class), free-before-copy equivalent. Not measured: wall time (timing-host jobs not run). Report: `handoff/TIMING-COV-REALLOC-GROW-NONAVX2-report.md`. |
| D-3.18 | §3.1 | — | **Small-class block index: one multiply for every class** (TIMING-COV-MALLOC-PAIR-CHAIN, 2026-11-06). Malloc's block offset stays `i * size` and free's block index stays `(off * magic) >> 40` with the start check `q * size == off`, for power-of-two classes too. A shift form for power-of-two classes (a `log2(size)` word in `FREE_VIEW`, a class-kind branch) was built and measured slower on the Haswell-EP class at default and hwcaps=-AVX2: +9 instructions and +1.4 to +1.7 cycles per malloc/free pair, heap_mix_real +7 to +9% cycles; without BMI2 a shift by a register count is 3 uops, and the shift-table load and class test add the rest. Reverted; the test `every_class_places_blocks_by_index_and_finds_them_again` (every class, indexes past one bitmap word, interior addresses at the alignment step) stays. Register: docs/saturation/04-allocator.md. |
| D-3.19 | §3.1 | — | **The heap's first reservation is one mapping** (HEAP-FIRST-USE, 2026-11-10). The first allocation of a process maps one range: the first segment (at its 16 MiB boundary), then one page holding generation 0 of the cache table, the segment bases and the segment hash, then the first 64 KiB cache chunk. Was five mappings (cache table 8 MiB, cache chunk, segment bases 8 MiB, segment hash 16 MiB, the segment), each registry page its own fault. Generation 0 of the segment registry is now at most 128 segments (2 GiB of slabs) and of the cache table at most 64 caches, with or without an address-space limit (amends D-3.14's "unlimited keeps the maxima"); later generations double as under D-3.14, so a heap past 2 GiB of slabs searches more than one hash generation on a registry lookup. If the one mapping fails, each part is mapped on its own as before; a first segment mapped for another NUMA node than the shard asking is left unused. Not changed: the `getcpu` shard choice on every slab refill (D-3.12). Tests: `the_first_allocation_reserves_one_mapping` (rt: one page request), `the_first_allocation_touches_few_pages` (core, `oracle/heap_first_faults.c`). |
| D-3.20 | §3.1 | — | **The heap asks the allowed-node set once, on its first slow path** (HEAP-FIRST-USE-2, 2026-11-10; coordinator ruling on #4168; fixes #4169). Amends D-3.12's "`Heap::set_numa(true)` is called at startup": nothing is asked at startup and nothing per allocation. The first time the heap chooses a cache or a slab (`Heap::shard_of`, slow paths only) it asks `Pages::allowed_nodes` once: in the product one `get_mempolicy(MPOL_F_MEMS_ALLOWED)` with a 1024-bit mask (`EINVAL`, a machine with nodes beyond the mask, counts as several; `ENOSYS` or any other refusal as one). More than one allowed node: NUMA placement turns on (as `Heap::set_numa(true)`) and the thread's node is read on slow paths exactly as D-3.12 says. One allowed node: shard 0, the kernel's default placement (first touch, optimal there), and the node is never read, so the vDSO `getcpu` is never resolved. An explicit `Heap::set_numa` before the first slow path takes the decision instead. Out of scope: a process whose allowed set changes after the first slow path (`set_mempolicy`, a cpuset move) keeps the decision taken then. The rseq `node_id` branch of D-3.12 is not wired in the product (the node read on several nodes is the vDSO `getcpu`); unchanged by this record. Tests (rt, the `Pages` trait's simulated topology): `one_allowed_node_never_reads_the_node`, `several_allowed_nodes_place_each_threads_slabs_on_its_node`. |
